utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Cosic, did you ever witness the entry of patients from Kaonik in the health centre? Do you know how they were brought in? Was it a passenger car or some other kind of vehicle? Do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: I think that Zlatko brought them in a car, in a passenger car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me if he would bring in -- bring them in himself or bring them one by one or several?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Sometimes -- at times he would bring two or one. That's as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you, perhaps, notice if those individuals were tied or handcuffed or something like that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, if you remember, what was the procedure of admission? How were they admitted to the health centre and then extended help? It is my understanding that there is a kind of waiting room or something like that in the health centre. Did they come into the waiting room or what?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Well, like everybody else. I mean, they would come and then Zlatko would talk to us, or a doctor, and tell him or us that he had brought them. And then we screened them. If it was something urgent, then we would admit them immediately or, if not, they waited like everybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that they waited in the waiting room together with other patients?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And tell us, who were those other patients?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Other patients. There were wounded or sick, like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let us talk for a while of this category of the wounded. Can you tell us who were those individuals? Were they civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: They were both civilians and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Were they HVO soldiers or some other soldiers? Could you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: They were HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And does it mean that at the same time, at the same place, in the waiting room of the health centre, the HVO soldiers and patients from Kaonik waited to be examined? Was it the normal situation? Was it uncommon?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: That was the usual situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you, perhaps, remember if some conflict -- if some incident ever broke out in the waiting room between these two groups of people?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Perhaps if they recognised each other, but we tried to take care and look to prevent it, to forestall it in time so as to prevent it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But did it ever happen?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Cosic, you had contact with Mr. Aleksovski. Do you remember what kind of clothes he wore? Was it some uniform or civilian clothes or how did he dress?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Well, sometimes he would be in a uniform and sometimes he would be in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if on the uniform, on those occasions when he wore a uniform, did he ever have any insignia or markings to indicate his membership in some military force?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it that you don't remember or that he didn't have any such markings?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: No, he did not have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Cosic, let's go back to those patients that you helped and who were brought from Kaonik. What were their complaints? What were their health problems that they had? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Mostly stomach disorders, as a rule. I cannot remember all the details, but that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So you remember they had some stomach disorders. Were there some other ailments or something else?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: No. Those were usually chronic diseases, chronic disorders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What kind of therapy did you administer to those cases?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Well, with documentation, if some of them had it, then we would see what was -- what ailment was about. If not, then the doctor would examine him and then decide on it. It was usually parenteral therapy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We are all layman. Could you please explain to us what does parenteral mean?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: I mean injections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Tell us, did these individuals have to come for control, for subsequent control after a period of therapy?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did they come for control examination?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And if there was any need for some -- for the medication, for medicines to be administered to those patients, how did that function?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Cosic, you said that, as far as the patients in the health centre were concerned, you had communication both with patients of Muslim origin and of Croat origin. Did you ever differentiate as regards the services that you extended to these two categories of patients?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you ever ask anyone, did you inquire of the ethnic origin of a patient?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Cosic, I mentioned the Kaonik facility. Did you visit at that facility ever?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was it before or after the conflict?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: During the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What took you there?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: It was a treatment. I had to apply the treatment prescribed by a doctor, and it had to be done in the prison. So I went there and gave a shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And where did it take place? What kind of a room?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: It was -- there was first a passage, and I think it was to the left, there was a room with guards and a man who, perhaps for an hour prior to my arrival -- I am saying that was the case, my impression at the time, who had been to the health centre and who had been examined in the health centre, and it had been decided that if he didn't feel well, that he would be given an injection and that a nurse would come. And all that was needed was for Zlatko to make a call. And that was how I went to the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, Mrs. Cosic, that patient that you are referring to, before your intervention, had been brought to the health centre for treatment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Then he was taken back to Kaonik. And after that you received a call from Mr. Aleksovski asking you to come and administer the treatment?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I see. And what was that building that you saw in Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. It was nighttime and I had not been to that place before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the interior of that building? You said there was a passage and that to the left there was a room with guards. Did you see any other rooms in that building?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And on that occasion did you have an opportunity to communicate with individuals who are in that building; I mean, those who were detained there? Could you communicate with them?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: No. No, I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity or did you see the atmosphere or the setting, the facilities in that building? I mean lighting, hygienic, sanitary conditions, things like that.

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: I was there for a very short while and I did not -- the conditions there did not seem to me all that bad. I mean, in view of the situation that we are all in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if that room that you were in, was it heated, was there any heating? Was it cold?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA STAPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, can you tell us how much longer you would need to complete your examination in chief, or shall we continue tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your lordships, I think it would be more advisable to adjourn for the day, continue tomorrow, simply because I do not want -- because I want to proceed at a normal pace. I do not really want to speed things unnecessarily up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. Very well, Mr. Mikulicic. We shall continue tomorrow at 9.00. No, I stand corrected. At 13.30, 1.30. Very well, we will be sitting at 1.30 p.m. until 5.30 p.m., the same time period of work, but tomorrow we will transfer that time period to the afternoon. That is all. See you tomorrow.
